body.statement:
For an admissible fixed choice of class constants with \(H=0\), \(p=S=d=1\), \(\lambda=\kappa=1\), and the uniform order-zero kernel \(K\), there is a triangular array of laws in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\), with \(n_1=N=T^2\), for which
\[
R_\star=T^{-2},\qquad
\lim_{T\to\infty}\mathbb E\!\left[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0\right]=\frac{3}{16}.
\]
In the same array, the event multiplier radius satisfies \(r_{\mathrm{tr}}=0\) almost surely even though the conditional variance of the centered event contribution is \(3/16\).
Moreover, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\),
\[
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
body.proof_tex:
It is enough to exhibit one admissible triangular array.  Throughout the proof, suppress the unique cohort index.  Fix
\[
H=0,\qquad p=S=d=1,\qquad \lambda=\kappa=1,
\qquad \pi_1=1,
\]
and choose
\[
B=16,\qquad c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1,
\qquad \delta_0=\frac14,
\qquad c_{\mathrm{mod}}=C_{\mathrm{mod}}=1.
\]
Take the H\"older radius \(L\) large enough to contain the affine regression defined below.  Let
\[
K(u)={\bf 1}\{|u|\leq1\}.
\]
Then \(r=\lceil\lambda\rceil-1=0\), \(b_0(u)=1\), and the normalized local-design threshold may be chosen with \(0<c_G\leq1\).  Let \(E_0\) be constant, set \(z_0=1/2\), and put \(\mathcal Z_+=\{1/2\}\).  For each integer \(T\geq1\), set
\[
n_1=N=T^2.
\]

We first construct the historical panel.  Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_T\) be independent uniform random variables on \([0,1]\), define
\[
m(x)=8+x-\frac12,
\qquad
Q_{ti}=m(X_t)+\frac12U_{ti},
\]
and take the variables \((U_{ti})_{t,i}\) to be independent Rademacher variables independent of the complete design.  Thus
\[
7\leq Q_{ti}\leq9\leq B,
\qquad
\mathbb E[Q_{ti}\mid X_t,E_0]=m(X_t).
\]
The first display verifies \(\texttt{ass:bounded-historical-wealth}\), and the second verifies \(\texttt{ass:historical-regression}\).  The affine map \(m\) is in \(\mathcal H_1(1,L)\), as required by \(\texttt{ass:holder-smoothness}\).  The conditional density is identically one, so \(\texttt{ass:design-density}\) holds.  Moreover, the design process \((X_t)_{t=1}^T\) is independent over calendar time.  Its conditional absolute-regularity coefficients therefore satisfy
\[
\beta_P(k\mid E_0)=0\leq\beta_0\rho_0^k,
\qquad k\geq1,
\]
which verifies the design-only version of \(\texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}\).  No condition on temporal dependence of the outcome path is needed for the proposition.

Independently of the entire panel, let
\[
Z_j=\frac12+V_j,
\]
where \(V_1,\ldots,V_N\) are independent Rademacher variables.  It follows that
\[
\mathbb E[Z_j\mid E_0]=z_0,
\qquad
\Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid E_0)=1,
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E\!left[|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)|^4\mid E_0\right]=1\leq B.
\]
Thus \(\texttt{ass:donor-independence}\), \(\texttt{ass:donor-replication}\), \(\texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}\), and \(\texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}\) hold.  Define \(X_t^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_t\), which verifies \(\texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates}\).

The local modulus can be evaluated exactly.  For \(0<\delta\leq\delta_0\), the perturbations \(z_0+u\) with \(|u|\leq\delta\) remain in \([0,1]\), and the definition of the full-covariance modulus gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\omega_P(\delta;z_0)
&=\sup_{|u|\leq\delta}|m(z_0+u)-m(z_0)|\\
&=\sup_{|u|\leq\delta}|u|=\delta.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves \(\texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus}\) with the displayed constants.  Also,
\[
\operatorname{dist}(z_0,\partial[0,1])=\frac12\geq\delta_0,
\qquad
P\{z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\}=1\geq c_X,
\]
so \(\texttt{ass:interior-event-path}\) and \(\texttt{ass:positive-query-region}\) hold.

We next construct the event outcomes.  Put
\[
G={\bf 1}\{X_1\leq1/4\},
\qquad
B_i(0)=8,
\qquad
B_i(1)=8+G,
\qquad
B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_i(1).
\]
Define \(B_i(a,\mathbf a_{-i})=B_i(a)\), and define every historical potential outcome \(Q_{ti}(a)\) to equal \(Q_{ti}\).  These definitions verify, respectively, \(\texttt{ass:consistency}\), \(\texttt{ass:historical-consistency}\), \(\texttt{ass:no-spillovers}\), and \(\texttt{ass:limited-anticipation}\).  They also imply
\[
0\leq B_i(a)\leq9\leq B,
\]
as required by \(\texttt{ass:bounded-event-wealth}\).  The construction is compatible with \(\texttt{def:buyhold-level}\): take \(W_{i,-1}=1\) and \(R_{i0}(a)=B_i(a)-1>-1\), so that
\[
W_{i,-1}\{1+R_{i0}(a)\}=B_i(a).
\]
Since \(m(z_0)=8\),
\[
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
\mathbb E[B_i(0)\mid z_0,E_0]=8=m(z_0),
\]
which proves \(\texttt{ass:event-transport}\).

Conditional on the complete design and \(E_0\), every \(B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is constant, while the historical path of unit \(i\) depends only on \((U_{ti})_{t=1}^T\).  The latter vectors are independent across \(i\).  Hence
\[
((Q_{ti})_{t=1}^T,B_i^{\mathrm{obs}})
\perp
((Q_{ti'})_{t=1}^T,B_{i'}^{\mathrm{obs}})
\mid (X_t)_{t=1}^T,E_0,
\qquad i\ne i',
\]
which is exactly \(\texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}\).  We have now checked every member property of the weakened class in \(\texttt{def:panel-law-class}\).  In particular, neither identical conditional response laws across units nor a response-variance lower bound was used.

Because \(z_0\) and \(E_0\) are constant and \(G\) is Bernoulli with success probability \(1/4\), \(\texttt{def:target}\) yields
\[
\tau_n(z_0)
=\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
\mathbb E[B_i(1)-B_i(0)\mid z_0,E_0]
=\mathbb E[G]=\frac14,
\]
whereas
\[
\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}=8+G.
\]

We now analyze the all-donor estimator in \(\texttt{def:feasible-estimator}\).  Let
\[
\bar Z=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N Z_j,
\qquad
\widetilde z=\Pi_{[0,1]}(\bar Z).
\]
Projection onto \([0,1]\) is nonexpansive and fixes \(z_0\).  Therefore
\[
|\widetilde z-z_0|
\leq|\bar Z-z_0|
=\left|N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NV_j\right|,
\]
and donor independence gives
\[
\mathbb E[(\widetilde z-z_0)^2\mid E_0]
\leq N^{-1}=T^{-2}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\), the initial bandwidth is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\underline h_T=h_{1,\beta}
&=C_h\left[(Tn_1)^{-1/3}
\vee\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}
\vee N^{-1/2}\right]\\
&=C_h\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T<1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Conditional on \(\widetilde z\in[0,1]\), the interval
\([\widetilde z-\underline h_T,\widetilde z+\underline h_T]\cap[0,1]\)
has Lebesgue measure at least \(\underline h_T\).  Define
\[
I_T=\{t:|X_t-\widetilde z|\leq\underline h_T\},
\qquad
\mathcal A_T=\{|I_T|>0\}.
\]
The uniform independent design and donor independence imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0,\widetilde z)
&\leq(1-\underline h_T)^T\\
&\leq\exp(-T\underline h_T),
\end{aligned}
\]
and consequently \(P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)\to0\).  On \(\mathcal A_T\), the degree-zero normalized Gram ratio at the initial bandwidth is
\[
\frac{G_1(\underline h_T)}{L_1(\underline h_T)}=1\geq c_G.
\]
Thus the selector chooses \(h_1=\underline h_T\), and its fitted intercept equals
\[
\widehat m_1
=\frac1{n_1|I_T|}
\sum_{t\in I_T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}Q_{ti}.
\]
The conditional-mean part obeys
\[
\left|
\frac1{|I_T|}\sum_{t\in I_T}m(X_t)-m(z_0)
\right|
\leq \underline h_T+|\widetilde z-z_0|,
\]
because \(|X_t-\widetilde z|\leq\underline h_T\) on \(I_T\) and \(m(x)-m(z_0)=x-z_0\).  Conditional on the design and donors, the regression-error part has mean zero and variance
\[
\operatorname{Var}\!\left(
\frac1{2n_1|I_T|}\sum_{t\in I_T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}U_{ti}
\,\middle|\,(X_t)_{t=1}^T,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^N
\right)
=\frac1{4n_1|I_T|}
\leq\frac1{4n_1}.
\]
Every successful degree-zero intercept lies in \([0,B]\), and the definition assigns zero after selector failure.  The preceding bounds and boundedness on \(\mathcal A_T^c\) therefore give a constant \(C<\infty\), independent of \(T\), such that
\[
\mathbb E[(\widehat m_1-m(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\leq C\left\{
\underline h_T^2+N^{-1}+n_1^{-1}
+P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)
\right\}\longrightarrow0.
\]

Using \(\widehat\tau=\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat m_1\), we obtain the exact decomposition
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=G-\frac14-\{\widehat m_1-m(z_0)\}.
\]
The last brace converges to zero in conditional \(L^2\).  By Cauchy--Schwarz, its cross term with the bounded variable \(G-1/4\) also converges to zero.  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
\lim_{T\to\infty}
\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
&=\mathbb E[(G-1/4)^2\mid E_0]\\
&=\frac14\left(1-\frac14\right)=\frac{3}{16}.
\end{aligned}
\]

For this array, every component in the iid-design comparator frontier of \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\) is equal to \(T^{-2}\):
\[
R_{\mathrm{tr}}=n_1^{-1}=T^{-2},
\]
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}=(Tn_1)^{-2/3}=(T^3)^{-2/3}=T^{-2},
\]
and
\[
R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-1}=T^{-2}.
\]
Therefore \(R_\star=T^{-2}\).

For the event multiplier calculation, all event outcomes have the common realized value \(8+G\).  Consequently
\[
E_{1i}=\frac1{n_1}
\{B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\}=0
\qquad(1\leq i\leq n_1).
\]
It follows from the definitions of \(G_{\mathrm{tr}}^{\#}\) and \(r_{\mathrm{tr}}\) that
\[
G_{\mathrm{tr}}^{\#}=0,
\qquad
r_{\mathrm{tr}}=0
\]
almost surely.  On the other hand, the centered event-average contribution is
\[
\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}
-\mathbb E[\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]
=G-\frac14,
\]
whose conditional variance is \(3/16\).

It remains to analyze \(C_\alpha\) from \(\texttt{def:honest-interval}\).  On \(\mathcal A_T\), the successful degree-zero weights are
\[
a_{ti}=\frac{{\bf 1}\{t\in I_T\}}{n_1|I_T|}.
\]
They are nonnegative and satisfy
\[
\sum_{t=1}^Ta_{ti}=\frac1{n_1},
\qquad
\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}a_{ti}=1.
\]
Thus the historical and event Hoeffding radii obey
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
&=B\left\{
\frac12\log\left(\frac2{\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}}\right)
n_1\left(\frac1{n_1}\right)^2
\right\}^{1/2}
=O(T^{-1}),\\
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
&=B\left\{
\frac12\log\left(\frac2{\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}}\right)
\frac1{n_1}
\right\}^{1/2}
=O(T^{-1}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The exact Taylor allowance satisfies
\[
\begin{aligned}
A_L
&=C_{0,1}L
\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
a_{ti}|X_t-\widetilde z|\\
&\leq C_{0,1}L\underline h_T
=O\!\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right).
\end{aligned}
\]

For the exact full-sample donor calibration, \(D=1\), and hence
\[
M_4(N)=\frac{16}{N}
+3\left(1-\frac1N\right)
=3+\frac{13}{N}\leq16.
\]
Therefore, for fixed \(\alpha\),
\[
q_N=\{M_4(N)/\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}\}^{1/4}=O(1),
\qquad
\delta_N=\sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,q_NN^{-1/2}=O(T^{-1}),
\]
and the upper local modulus gives
\[
A_{\mathrm{don}}=C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta_N^\kappa=O(T^{-1}).
\]
In particular, \(\delta_N\leq\delta_0\) for every sufficiently large \(T\).  On \(\mathcal A_T\), the selected Gram matrix is positive and all weights and radii are finite.  Thus, under the all-donor construction, none of the declared bad-sample conditions occurs on \(\mathcal A_T\) for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Combining the four radius bounds yields
\[
H_\alpha{\bf 1}_{\mathcal A_T}
=O\!\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right)=o(1),
\qquad
P(\text{bad sample}\mid E_0)
\leq P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)\longrightarrow0.
\]

Finally,
\[
\widehat\tau-G=8-\widehat m_1\longrightarrow0
\]
in conditional probability, while \(|G-1/4|\geq1/4\) almost surely.  On \(\mathcal A_T\), if
\[
|\widehat\tau-G|<\frac1{16}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
H_\alpha<\frac18,
\]
then
\[
|\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)|
\geq |G-1/4|-|\widehat\tau-G|
\geq\frac3{16}>H_\alpha,
\]
so \(\tau_n(z_0)\notin C_\alpha\).  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}
&\leq P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)
+P\{|\widehat\tau-G|\geq1/16\mid E_0\}\\
&\quad+P\{H_\alpha\geq1/8,\mathcal A_T\mid E_0\}
\longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves every assertion of the proposition.
